paper_metadata.title: Longitudinal Assessment of White Matter Abnormalities Following Sports-Related Concussion

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a well-defined target population of NCAA Division I athletes. Recruitment and diagnostic criteria for concussion are clearly described and follow international guidelines. While there is a slight trend toward more prior concussions in the CA group, the groups are generally well-matched for age, education, and sport type.

quips_assessment.goal: Goal: To judge the risk of attrition bias (likelihood that relationship between PF and outcome are different for completing and non-completing participants).
quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: There is a notable decline in sample size from T1 (n=33) to T3 (n=26) for the concussed group. While the reasons for dropout are not explicitly detailed, the use of Linear Mixed-Effects models helps mitigate the impact of missing data on the longitudinal analysis.

items.reasoning: Approximately 65% of the initial concussed cohort (26/40) completed the final T3 visit, which is acceptable but indicates some attrition.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.goal: Goal: To judge the risk of measurement bias related to how PF was measured (differential measurement of PF related to the level of outcome).
quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factor (DTI/FA) is measured using standardized, objective neuroimaging protocols. The study uses advanced processing techniques (AFNI, FSL) and accounts for motion artifacts, which are critical for DTI reliability.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: One commonly assessed DTI metric is fractional anisotropy (FA), which measures the direction of water diffusion along white matter tracts... MRI was performed using a General Electric Healthcare Discovery MR750 3-Tesla
items.reasoning: FA is clearly defined and the technical parameters for its measurement are detailed.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: A previously described binary classification scheme was used to flag individual gradients with excessive motion or zipper artifacts... Head motion during DTI scan acquisition was calculated
items.reasoning: The use of 3T MRI and rigorous motion correction/artifact flagging ensures high measurement reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: scalar measures of axial diffusivity (AD), radial diffusivity (RD), and fractional anisotropy (FA)... voxel-wise analyses were also performed
items.reasoning: FA is treated as a continuous variable in both ROI and voxel-wise analyses.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: MRI was performed using a General Electric Healthcare Discovery MR750 3-Tesla whole body MRI scanner... for all participants.
items.reasoning: All participants were scanned using the same equipment and protocol.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: DTI and anatomical imaging data were collected on 46/46 HA, 29/33 T1, 28/30 T2 and 24/ 26 T3 participants.
items.reasoning: The majority of participants who attended visits provided usable DTI data.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Linear mixed-effects (LME) models... a random intercept was used to account for missing data
items.reasoning: LME is a standard and appropriate statistical approach for handling missing data in longitudinal studies without requiring simple imputation.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: PF Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.goal: Goal: To judge the risk of bias related to the measurement of outcome (differential measurement of outcome related to the baseline level of PF).
quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a mix of objective cognitive tests and subjective symptom scales. A significant risk is noted for the mood assessments (HAM-A/D) as the interviewers were not blinded to the concussion status, which could introduce bias.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Structured interviews for the Hamilton Depression and Anxiety Rating Scales served as the primary behavioral measures... return-to-play decision (days)
items.reasoning: Outcomes include validated clinical scales and a real-world metric (return-to-play).

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: structured interviewers were not blinded to concussion diagnoses, and thus potential interviewer bias cannot be ruled out.
items.reasoning: While the scales are valid, the lack of blinding for the primary behavioral outcome (HAM-A/D) is a methodological weakness.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The Automated Neuropsychological Assessment Metrics 4 Sports Medicine Battery (ANAM) was used to collect secondary measures... for all participants.
items.reasoning: Standardized computerized and interview-based assessments were applied consistently.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.goal: Goal: To judge the risk of bias due to confounding (i.e. the effect of PF is distorted by another factor that is related to PF and outcome).
quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a healthy contact-sport control group to account for subconcussive impacts and athlete lifestyle. However, the CA group had a trend toward more prior concussions, and the analysis does not explicitly adjust for this or other potential confounders (like medication use) in the primary DTI models.

items.reasoning: Key demographic and clinical confounders were recorded.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Confounding Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Important potential confounders are appropriately accounted for, limiting potential bias with respect to the relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.goal: Goal: To judge the risk of bias related to the statistical analysis and presentation of results.
quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical approach is sophisticated, using LME for longitudinal data and Monte Carlo simulations for multiple comparison corrections in neuroimaging. The reporting is transparent regarding both significant and non-significant findings.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Linear mixed-effects (LME) models with time as a fixed factor... Monte Carlo simulations (10,000 iterations) determined the necessary correction
items.reasoning: The analytical steps for both behavioral and imaging data are well-documented.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: To limit the number of comparisons... composite measures of ANAM scores were calculated... LME models with time as a fixed factor
items.reasoning: The use of composite scores and LME is theoretically sound for longitudinal clinical studies.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: LME... a random intercept was used to account for missing data with compound symmetry as the covariance structure.
items.reasoning: LME is the gold standard for longitudinal designs with missing data points.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Analyses of individual ANAM measures can be found in the Supplement to ensure that data reduction did not result in a loss of critical information.
items.reasoning: The authors provide supplemental data and report non-significant trends (e.g., tau results), suggesting low risk of selective reporting.
